quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: During a normal turn, what should happen?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should not lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: During a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle should lean together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider keeps their body more upright to balance the bike.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcyclist under normal conditions?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum two-second following distance under normal conditions. In poor weather or bad road conditions, increase your following distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic lanes are merging ahead.

questions.question: Which part of the lane is safest?

options.text: Always the left portion of the lane.
Always the right portion of the lane.
It depends on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position based on traffic, road conditions, and what is around you.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: You are passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This keeps you away from opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane for safety.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle's acceleration and braking change?

options.text: It takes less time to stop and speed up.
It takes the same time as normal.
It takes more time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows down acceleration and braking. With a passenger, your motorcycle responds more slowly to your commands than when you ride alone.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling under 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space and proceed slowly. Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see emergency lights.

questions.question: What happens when you lock your brakes?

options.text: It helps in most situations.
It improves steering.
It causes control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes control problems.
questions.explanation: Locked brakes reduce control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcycle rider has an advantage over a car driver because:

options.text: A motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
The rider can stay on the left side of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
Motorcycles can stop in a shorter distance than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can stay on the left side of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid opening car doors, people getting out of cars, and people stepping between parked vehicles. Only use the left part of the lane if no cars are coming toward you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface ahead
Other traffic around you
Conditions that look the same as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that look the same as you approach
questions.explanation: Look ahead for problems on the road. Make a plan to stay safe.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.

options.text: On the highway
Near an intersection
In a group

questions.correctAnswerText: Near an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. At an intersection, position yourself in your lane so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointing downward with your toes.
Relaxed and loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as on your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Learn how it works in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how it works in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding it in a safe area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther away.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you feel most comfortable.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: The left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This position helps you avoid opened car doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a single file line.
Ride in pairs.
Stagger their positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stagger their positions.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding through curves, or entering or leaving a road.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots.
Are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors only. Look over your shoulder only if something seems wrong.
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no other vehicles are in your path. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
